item.title: Dev Sentinel Story 2: Architecting Dev Sentinel - Evolving AI Agent Failures into Reusable Experience
item.description:
Architecting Dev Sentinel: Evolving AI Agent Failures into Reusable Experience

In Part I, I explored the philosophy of “Struggle Equity”: how failures and missteps are the raw materials of senior engineering intuition. AI coding agents like Claude Code iterate at lightning speed, but they lack this long-term architectural intuition.

An agent can retry a flawed architectural approach multiple times across different sessions without ever accumulating pattern awareness. It treats every ModuleNotFoundError or infinite recursion as an isolated incident.

item.title: Dev Sentinel Story 1: We fail every day, but that failure becomes the success of our next attempt
item.description:
We fail every day, but that failure becomes the success of our next attempt

“We fail every day, but that failure becomes the success of our next attempt.”

Failure Repeats

Not long ago, a production incident occurred in a service I operate.

An SQS-triggered Lambda handler processed a single event that spawned an excessive number of DynamoDB transactions in parallel. Eventually, the Lambda hit its timeout limit.

item.title: Agentic Software Engineering (ASE): The Software Development Landscape is Shifting Again
item.description:
This is a picture drawn by AI

Agentic Software Engineering (ASE): The Software Development Landscape is Shifting Again

These days, we often hear stories like “Successful CI/CD Automation with a Coding Agent” or “An MVP for a side project completed in just a few days.” It’s becoming clear that AI agents are moving beyond being mere assistants and are diving deep into the actual development workflow.
